lines: At one time the Buddha was staying near Rājagaha in the Bamboo Grove, the squirrels’ feeding ground.
“Mendicants, the lifespan of humans is short.
We are headed for lives to come. We must do what is skillful, we must practice the spiritual life.
A long life is a hundred years or a little more.”
Then Māra the Wicked went up to the Buddha and addressed him in verse:
“The days and nights don’t rush by,
The life of mortals keeps rolling on,
like a chariot’s rim around the hub.”
and then life is cut short.
The life of mortals wastes away,
like the water in tiny streams.”
Then Māra the Wicked, thinking, “The Buddha knows me! The Holy One knows me!” miserable and sad, vanished right there.
